questions.prompt: What were Luca and Fern moving?

stimulus.title: The borrowed cart
stimulus.body: Luca and Fern had to move books from the office to the school library. The caretaker lent them a garden cart. Luca made one tall pile, but a few books slid onto the grass when the cart turned. Fern suggested three lower piles instead. Ahead, a step blocked the cart's small wheels. They could unload everything and lift the cart, or take the longer path around the back of the building. They chose the smooth back path. The other helpers arrived first, but Luca and Fern delivered every book clean and dry. Luca decided to check the path before loading next time.

questions.explanation: The first sentence identifies the books they had to move.

questions.prompt: Where is the seed shelf?

stimulus.title: The seed shelf
stimulus.body: Our class has a seed shelf beside the door. Each envelope lists the plant's name and the month the seeds were collected. A leaf drawing helps us recognise the plant. Ask the garden helper before borrowing an envelope. Write your name and the plant's name in the green book. Take seeds home in a dry bag, and tell the helper if an envelope is wet. A pot needs holes so extra water can drain away. Follow the soil instructions on the envelope. Record what happens; a drawing is fine. If a plant grows well, you may save some of its seeds for the shelf. If it does not grow, bring your record back anyway. We can learn from that too.

questions.explanation: The opening sentence places the shelf beside the door.

questions.prompt: What was the usual packing-up signal?

stimulus.title: The quiet bell
stimulus.body: Amira usually rang a small bell when garden club needed to pack up. One afternoon, a bird landed on the fence nearby. Amira put down the bell and raised her hand. The other children noticed and raised their hands too. She whispered the packing-up instructions. They moved the tool box and seed trays into the shed without walking towards the bird. After the last tray was put away, the bird flew to a high branch. The next day, Amira drew a raised hand on a card and placed it beside the bell. The club now had a quiet signal as well as a ringing one.

questions.explanation: Amira usually rang a small bell.

questions.prompt: Where was Owen planning to use his boat?

stimulus.title: Boat on the veranda
stimulus.body: Owen folded a paper boat for the class water tray and wrote his name underneath. On the way to school, the boat slipped against his wet raincoat. One corner became damp. Owen put the boat on a dry bench on the veranda. His teacher placed scrap paper underneath it. After morning reading, Owen checked the boat. It was dry, but the damp corner had bent. In the tray it floated close to the edge instead of moving straight ahead. Owen left it out of the distance race. He made a tiny paper flag, and his boat carried the flag beside the starting line. It still had a useful job.

questions.explanation: The boat was folded for the class water tray.
